messages:
maya: heads-up: we're getting a 5xx/timeouts spike for hosted inference in eu-west starting ~12:07. customer reports + monitoring alerting. opening warroom.
sam: seeing lots of 502/504 from gateway logs, correlated with large token requests from a single client id. early hypothesis: upstream overload + auth hiccups.
lee: +1, graphs show p95 request latency to runtime jumping from 70ms -> 2.4s and then 5xx rate rising. KV cache hit-rate dropped at same time.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT STARTED by maya at 2024-06-13T12:09Z — channel linked: #incidents — incident id: INC-20240613-77
support-ali: queued 8 external customer tickets so far. most mention `timeout` and `broken pipe` in the client logs. one included a reproducible curl to /v1/generate.
eng-runtime-jordan: can we get a minimal repro? Ali, can you paste the curl and the client headers they used (esp auth/billing headers)?
support-ali: pasted —

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-XXXX" \
  -H "X-Cust-Billing: acct_999999999" \
  -d '{"model":"rwdl-13b", "input":"<large prompt>"}'
```
maya: deploy-bot shows a config rollout at 12:05 (small routing change to edge-proxy). could be related.
deploy-bot: Rollout: edge-proxy v3.14 -> v3.15 at 2024-06-13T12:05Z by ci/cd. Canary passed.
sre-elena: checking edge logs now. I'm seeing repeated `upstream prematurely closed connection` from nginx + `413 header too large` occasionally for same requests.
lee: 413 header too large? curious. That could be interaction with billing header size or embed of long metadata.
eng-runtime-jordan: runtime shows lots of rejected connections due to kv-cache misses and then backlog. Also seeing auth-service returning 502 intermittently for token introspection.
maya: so two things in flight: edge rollout + auth token introspection flakiness + large billing header sizes — could be causing connection resets and downstream queue blowup.
sam: immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback edge-proxy to v3.14 2) throttle large requests by size at gateway 3) enable model-fallback to smaller variant for busy routes.
marta: I can do a fast rollback to v3.14, ready if we decide.
sre-elena: let's rollback edge first to confirm. it's the smallest blast radius. sam — coordinate.
sam: initiating rollback now.
deploy-bot: Rollback started: edge-proxy v3.15 -> v3.14 at 2024-06-13T12:14Z by sam. Canary in progress.
lee: while rollback is running, I'll open an auth-service investigation. Jordan, can you isolate requests that show `X-Cust-Billing` length > 2k?
eng-runtime-jordan: yes pulling logs filtered by header length and 5xx. sample: `upstream: http://runtime:8080, host: runtime-1, request: POST /v1/generate, upstream_status: 502, req_headers_len: 2310`
support-ali: customers often add detailed prompt metadata in X-Cust-Billing for billing attribution; some of those payloads are large.
sre-elena: rollback complete. metrics: 5xx rate halved within 2 minutes, p95 latency improving. still above normal.
maya: good rollback signal. keep monitoring. we still need root cause — auth + header sizes.
eng-runtime-jordan: reproduced locally: long header causes edge nginx to reject with 413, but some client libs retry and flood backend before client sees rejection, causing auth-service bursts and token-introspect timeouts. sequence: 1) client sends large header 2) edge returns 413 3) client retries with exponential backoff but jitter low -> many concurrent retries 4) auth-service overloaded -> 502 -> runtime saturates -> 5xx wave.
lee: noted. Actionable short-term: patch edge nginx to reject earlier and return consistent 413 without proxying; add stricter `client_max_body_size`/`large_client_header_buffers` in edge; add token introspect rate limit and circuit-breaker.
marta: I'll raise a config PR to enforce `large_client_header_buffers 8 16k` and add response header telling customers about header size limit.
sam: support-ali, please draft a customer message: explain we saw timeouts tied to large billing headers and retries, mitigation done (edge rollback) and next steps.
support-ali: drafting now, will share in 15.
sre-elena: long-term items: (A) add instrumentation to measure header lengths and correlate with 5xx, (B) build a buffered queue in front of auth-service with backpressure + 429, (C) improve SDK client retry jitter/backoff recommendations in docs.
maya: let's capture action items and owners. I'll summarize.
maya: SUMMARY ACTION ITEMS:
- edge: enforce larger buffer + immediate 413 handling + customer-facing header limit doc (owner: marta) — ETA: 48h
- auth: add token-introspect circuit-breaker and rate-limits, plus alerting on introspect latencies (owner: lee) — ETA: 72h
- runtime: add guard to reject requests when kv-cache misses cross threshold and emit `X-Rejected-Due-To` header (owner: jordan) — ETA: 5 days
- ops: create dashboard showing header length distribution and 5xx correlation (owner: sre-elena) — ETA: 3 days
- docs/support: customer comms + recommended header size and SDK retry guidelines (owner: support-ali) — ETA: 24h
- postmortem: assign follow-up writeup, include timeline and RCA (owner: maya) — ETA: 3 days
marta: starting PR now, linking to this thread.
support-ali: customer message posted to affected accounts draft: "We observed a transient service disruption caused by unusually large request metadata headers and follow-up retries that caused auth introspection to saturate. We've rolled back an edge change and implemented mitigations; engineers are rolling out permanent fixes. We're available to help remove long metadata if needed." will send after legal review.
eng-runtime-jordan: throwing one repro snippet in case folks want to test quickly:

```
# stress client that sends large header
for i in {1..50}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test" \
    -H "X-Cust-Billing: $(python -c 'print("A"*2500)')" \
    -d '{"model":"rwdl-13b","input":"hi"}' &
done
```
lee: thanks. adding an alert rule to pager for `auth.introspect.latency > 200ms` and `edge.413-rate > 0.1%`.
sre-elena: created dashboard and added to incident board.
maya: final: good containment. continue action items. we'll meet at 16:00 for postmortem draft check-in. thanks everyone :clap:
